idiom_name: companion object factory function (companion object { fun of(...) })
implementation_notes: kotlinlang documents companion objects as the idiomatic place for factory methods: companion object Factory { fun create(): MyClass } or a top-level function replaces the classic Creator subclass, and because a factory function is not a constructor it may return a cached instance, a subtype hidden behind an interface, or null where construction can fail - exactly what listOf and lazy do in the standard library. Sealed interfaces plus an exhaustive when give the closed-set form of the same function with compiler-checked coverage; the classic protected abstract create() in an abstract class remains available and is used when a framework subclasses the creator. Note that a companion object is an instance of the companion, not a static member: annotate with @JvmStatic if Java callers must see a static method.
pitfalls: A companion object initializes when its class is first resolved, so a factory that populates state in the companion can observe half-initialized collaborators; keep registration explicit and lazy.
Companion-level mutable caches are process-wide globals: they need synchronization (or an immutable map built at initialization) and they leak between tests.
Default arguments and overloads already cover many 'named constructor' needs; a factory function that only forwards its arguments to the constructor duplicates the API surface for no gain.
An `operator fun invoke` in the companion makes Type(value) read like a constructor but is considered less idiomatic and complicates reflection (Companion::invoke), so prefer a named function.
